definitions.explanation: Being alone or going somewhere without companions. Often refers specifically to living or working away from one's family.

examples.japanese: {単身|たんしん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{海外|かいがい}→海外：00134_kaigai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{渡|わた}った→渡る：02441_wataru⟧。
⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大阪|おおさか}→大阪：09779_oosaka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{単身赴任|たんしんふにん}→単身赴任：18620_tanshinfunin⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: My father is on a solo work transfer in Osaka.

examples.japanese: {単身|たんしん}{世帯|せたい}{向|む}け⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦マンション→マンション：01035_manshon⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: Apartments for single-person households are increasing.

notes:
{単身|たんしん} can function as both a noun and an adverb. It is commonly used in compound expressions related to living or working alone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{単身赴任|たんしんふにん}→単身赴任：18620_tanshinfunin⟧ (solo work transfer — living apart from family for work)
- {単身|たんしん}{世帯|せたい} (single-person household)
- {単身|たんしん}{者|しゃ} (a person living alone)
- {単身|たんしん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{乗|の}り{込|こ}む→乗り込む：04618_norikomu⟧ (to go in alone)

USAGE:
⟦{単身赴任|たんしんふにん}→単身赴任：18620_tanshinfunin⟧ is one of the most frequently used compounds. It refers to the common Japanese practice where a worker is transferred to a distant office and lives alone while the family stays behind, typically so that children can continue at the same school.
